A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiCE research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v3 reports original counterfactual-generation experiments on GMSC, Adult and German Credit, including validity, plausibility, similarity, sparsity and runtime results.

after.justification: v4 retains original real-data experiments and adds SPN approximation measurements, synthetic counterfactual experiments and distribution-estimation evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix F.1 introduces LiCE (sample), which sets the likelihood threshold to the minimum of the factual's likelihood and the training median. This adds an adaptive threshold rule to the retained SPN/MIO method; its main architecture, distance-likelihood objective and desiderata constraints remain.

E1.justification: The three real-world datasets are retained. v4 adds synthetic distributions from eight Bayesian networks for density-estimation evaluation (G.4), including counterfactual-generation tasks on asia, alarm and win95pts (F.4). These introduce substantial coverage of scenarios with known generating probabilities.

E2.justification: The external baseline roster remains DiCE, VAE, C-CHVAE, both FACE variants and PROPLACE; PlaCE and DACE remain unevaluated. Within the matched variant comparison, LiCE (sample) is added (v3 Table 9 versus v4 Table 10). The runtime comparison also gains quartile and sample variants (v3 Table 10 versus v4 Table 12).

E3.justification: The original preprocessing, neural-network architecture and five-fold design are retained. v4 adds comparisons on common successful factuals, synthetic CE experiments using 10,000 training samples and 100 fresh factuals, and density evaluation using 1,000 test samples. New metrics include true generating probabilities and density-fit measures. Synthetic optimizing LiCE uses alpha = 1, whereas the real-data experiments retain 0.1.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's variant and runtime comparisons, v4 tests MIO approximation accuracy against the actual SPN output (Table 2), compares methods on common factuals (F.2), evaluates CEs against known probabilities (F.4), and assesses SPN distribution fidelity (G.4). The sample-threshold variant also extends the sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: v3 already reports standard deviations and five-fold experiments. v4 adds five-seed synthetic experiments, Friedman and Nemenyi significance tests with critical-difference diagrams, and significance tests for density correlations. F.4 aggregates synthetic runs, while G.4 explicitly selects the best-performing SPN from five fits.

E6.justification: Many retained benchmark and runtime values are revised. For example, LiCE (optimize) Credit NLL changes from 30.3 ± 3.8 to 28.8 ± 3.3, and LiCE (median) GMSC success changes from 53.6% to 60.0%. v4 also adds approximation, synthetic-probability, ranking and correlation results. These are revised and additional reports, rather than demonstrated controlled performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: v4 supplies explicit binary/big-M inequalities for sum-node maximization and an argument for tightness under likelihood maximization (Section 4), replacing v3's solver-level max expression. It removes the assertion that hard-EM training makes the approximation exact and adds formulation-size reasoning in F.3. The existing log-sum-exp bound and most other mathematics remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution lists retain the same principal claims: an MIO formulation of SPNs, SPN likelihood as a plausibility measure, and LiCE for producing plausible, close and sparse counterfactuals satisfying common desiderata. Causality receives less main-text emphasis but its formulation and claimed support remain in the appendices.

C2.justification: v4 substantially qualifies reliance on SPN likelihood. F.4 discusses lost statistical superiority under successful-factual comparisons and poor win95pts rankings; G.4 suggests insufficient training coverage as an explanation for weaker andes density estimates. It also expands explanations of threshold tradeoffs and infeasible Credit cases, beyond v3's emphasis on computational overhead and possible numerical failures.

D1.justification: v4 specifies the sum-node big-M constant as 100 and documents the bnlearn software, target variables and sampling procedures for the new synthetic experiments. The rough total compute estimate rises from 15,000 to 20,000 CPU hours. Most original hyperparameters and hardware details remain; the repository was already linked in v3.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands research positioning through comparisons with adversarial-random-forest and GAN approaches, CeFlow, PPCEF and diffeomorphic counterfactuals. Section 3 and G.3 develop the distinctions between SPNs, GMMs, flows, autoregressive models and autoencoders, particularly categorical-data support and compatibility with linear MIO formulations.

P1.justification: The introduction, method exposition and results discussion are extensively revised. Prerequisites become separate from related work, and v3's single nested Appendix A becomes thematic Appendices A–G. Existing causality, diversity and encoding material is redistributed, and unfinished editorial notes in v3's supplementary discussion are removed.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a substantially different conference layout, transposes and revises Table 1, and redraws Figure 1 with a different example and explicit likelihood clipping. It adds approximation and common-factual tables, synthetic evaluation tables, critical-difference diagrams and an eight-panel density-fit figure. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 evaluates plausibility primarily through the same SPN used by LiCE and acknowledges that methods succeed on different factuals. v4 substantially addresses these weaknesses through known-probability synthetic evaluations, common-factual comparisons, direct approximation checks and statistical analyses. It also reports unfavorable findings that clarify dependence on SPN quality. Best-of-five selection in the density study and weak win95pts results limit generality, but the added validation and more explicit limitations substantially improve the paper's evidential quality.
